title: Utility difficulty sits beside different work-change surfaces for renters and owners
source_unit: 2025 SIPP public-use file, 2024 reference year; identified person-month pairs with utility-payment difficulty and tenure at month t, followed by earnings or hours change at month t+1

observations.period: 2024 reference year; utility difficulty and owned/bought tenure at month t

denominator.unit: eligible adjacent person-month pairs; earnings and hours retain separate valid-pair universes

earnings_changed_next_month.unit: person-weighted percent; valid pair n=4414; Fay-BRR SE 1.684 pp; 95% CI 77.184–83.785

hours_changed_next_month.unit: person-weighted percent; valid pair n=4508; Fay-BRR SE 0.707 pp; 95% CI 6.224–8.996

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month transition using EAWBGAS=1, ETENURE=1, WPFINWGT at month t, and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5; THHLDSTATUS and AAWBGAS validity filters retained.
observations.uncertainty: The utility field is a reported household/reference-person condition and not a dated bill shock. Person-month rows repeat household fields; estimates are not household prevalence. The comparison is descriptive and outcome universes differ.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE code 1: owned or being bought.
observations.counterinterpretation: Utility difficulty may reflect income, health, season, household composition, local prices, or job conditions; tenure does not identify which mechanism explains the following-month movement.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; utility difficulty and rented tenure at month t

denominator.unit: eligible adjacent person-month pairs; earnings and hours retain separate valid-pair universes

earnings_changed_next_month.unit: person-weighted percent; valid pair n=4638; Fay-BRR SE 1.429 pp; 95% CI 79.661–85.261

hours_changed_next_month.unit: person-weighted percent; valid pair n=4738; Fay-BRR SE 0.643 pp; 95% CI 6.322–8.844

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month transition using EAWBGAS=1, ETENURE=2, WPFINWGT at month t, and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5; THHLDSTATUS and AAWBGAS validity filters retained.
observations.uncertainty: The estimate is a descriptive tenure-conditioned transition screen, not evidence that renting or utility difficulty caused work change. Person-month rows and separate outcome universes remain explicit.
observations.counterinterpretation: The renter comparison may reflect different income, local prices, family composition, provider access, job mix, or seasonal exposure rather than a tenure mechanism.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no utility difficulty and owned/bought tenure at month t

denominator.unit: eligible adjacent person-month pairs; earnings and hours retain separate valid-pair universes

earnings_changed_next_month.unit: person-weighted percent; valid pair n=104742; Fay-BRR SE 0.291 pp; 95% CI 83.802–84.942

hours_changed_next_month.unit: person-weighted percent; valid pair n=105911; Fay-BRR SE 0.133 pp; 95% CI 4.666–5.188

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month transition using EAWBGAS=2, ETENURE=1, WPFINWGT at month t, and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5; THHLDSTATUS and AAWBGAS validity filters retained.
observations.uncertainty: The no-difficulty group is a descriptive comparison surface; it does not provide a counterfactual for utility difficulty or control for job, season, health, or household differences.
observations.subgroup: ETENURE code 1: owned or being bought.
observations.counterinterpretation: Lower hours movement without reported utility difficulty may reflect job composition or selection rather than utility stability protecting work continuity.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no utility difficulty and rented tenure at month t

denominator.unit: eligible adjacent person-month pairs; earnings and hours retain separate valid-pair universes

earnings_changed_next_month.unit: person-weighted percent; valid pair n=38614; Fay-BRR SE 0.535 pp; 95% CI 82.424–84.522

hours_changed_next_month.unit: person-weighted percent; valid pair n=38801; Fay-BRR SE 0.241 pp; 95% CI 5.488–6.432

observations.method: Same-person adjacent-month transition using EAWBGAS=2, ETENURE=2, WPFINWGT at month t, and 240 replicate weights with Fay BRR, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5; THHLDSTATUS and AAWBGAS validity filters retained.
observations.uncertainty: The comparison retains separate field universes and is not a causal tenure or utility estimate.
observations.counterinterpretation: Renter and owner differences may reflect selection, work type, geography, resources, or household composition; unchanged hours do not identify desired hours or security.

related_sources.claim: The unconditioned utility-to-following-work screen and its full-file reproduction are preserved as the parent comparison.
The tenure/resource layer supplies the housing and utility exposure context.
The official dictionary defines EAWBGAS, ETENURE, TPEARN, and TMWKHRS fields and status codes.

boundary: This is a same-person monthly descriptive transition conditioned on utility-payment difficulty and tenure. It does not establish a dated bill shock, a tenure effect, utility causation, desired hours, job quality, care substitution, recovery, trust, political action, or household prevalence. It is a conditional work-transition layer, not a complete housing/energy episode.
